sample_unit: participants (214 oropharyngeal cancer cases and 433 controls)
models_evaluated: US-developed oropharyngeal cancer risk prediction model

links.outcome: External validation of US-developed OPC risk model on Canadian data: overall performance, discrimination, calibration
links.effect: Above-average overall performance (Somers delta 0.49; scaled Brier 68.8%) and discrimination (C-statistic 0.74), but suboptimal calibration (calibration-in-the-large 4.93; slope 0.57).
links.quote: The model showed above-average overall performance (Somers delta score, 0.49; scaled Brier score, 68.8%; Nagelkerke R2, 0.2) and discrimination (concordance statistic, 0.74; discrimination slope, 0.18), but calibration was suboptimal (calibration-in-the-large, 4.93; calibration slope, 0.57).

links.outcome: Need for local recalibration of externally developed model
links.effect: Calibration was suboptimal in the Canadian dataset (calibration-in-the-large 4.93; slope 0.57), so recalibration using Canadian data is warranted.
links.quote: Therefore, recalibration using a Canadian dataset is warranted.

screen.reason: Evaluates the transportability/external validation of an existing US-derived clinical risk prediction model to a Canadian population cohort, assessing discrimination and calibration issues prior to clinical adoption.
